Using power responsibly

More help from machines. More say for people.

Let machines help with the work while people keep a meaningful say in what is made.

A design philosophy with a small working example

AI can help write software, suggest changes and run checks. People still decide what is worth making, who it serves and whether it is good.

The aim is to make a system’s workings understandable and changeable. You should be able to follow an idea back to its source and ask what was checked. The workshop lets you try this with two small edits.

Words used here
authorship
Having a meaningful say in what is made, why it is made and how it is changed.
Read the fuller explanation

The aim is to let AI take on more programming work while people retain expertise, taste, discretion and responsibility. People decide what is worth making, who it serves and whether the experience is good.

Open architecture should mean more than being handed source code. It should let you understand the decisions, follow a value to its source, challenge a rule and change the workings. The architecture should remain revisable.

Assurance should fit the consequences. A typed check, an automated test, a human review and independent verification are different kinds of evidence. We should say which happened, against which version, and what remains unknown.

AI can remain a collaborator throughout. The intention is to make expertise go further; any claim about productivity or jobs would need evidence of its own.

Where this comes from: People choosing; machines helping

Product philosophy · inspectable example

A design philosophy with a small working example

The workshop lets you edit two values and follow the results through the existing checking system. It is not a complete authoring environment or independent verification.

Read the full source note

Human authorship, assisted by AI

Developed with Aaron in the Encounter discussion: remove unnecessary labour, preserve human authorship, and make consequences and evidence inspectable. Autonomy, human taste and risk-appropriate assurance are design commitments. The accompanying example executes a bounded typed edit through the existing Temple kernel. Its checks do not establish independent verification, a complete authoring environment, employment outcomes or a measured productivity multiplier.

This account is drawn from Aaron’s own words; it is not an independent account of anyone else’s experience.
